diagnosis.summary: Run afd3a24b failed at ingest because upstream added a new column, coupon_code, to orders.csv for 2026-10-01. All 7 contract columns are present and unchanged, so nothing is renamed or missing. I proposed ignore_extra_columns(orders, [coupon_code]), then a rerun.

root_cause.explanation: The landing orders.csv for 2026-10-01 has an extra trailing column, coupon_code, that is not in the raw.orders contract. Ingest is strict about the header and rejected the file with 'missing columns [], unexpected columns [coupon_code]'. The 09-30 and 09-29 runs succeeded, and the ingest config is empty, so nothing handles the new column.

evidence.claim: Ingest failed on raw.orders with an unexpected column coupon_code and no missing columns.
The landing header has all 7 contract columns in order plus coupon_code. Nothing is renamed or missing. The ingest config has no handling for the column.
Per the runbook, an unexpected column with no missing column is a new upstream column. The fix is ignore_extra_columns followed by a rerun.
The earlier runs for 09-30 and 09-29 succeeded.

alternatives_considered: apply_column_mapping: rejected because no contract column is missing, so this isn't a rename.
request_upstream_redelivery: rejected because the change looks deliberate and persistent, not a one-off bad file.
revert_model_change: rejected because the failure is at ingest, before any dbt model runs.
rerun_only: rejected because the header mismatch would fail again.

escalate: not needed, since the contract columns are unchanged. I could only see 4 of 440 coupon_code values (all empty), so a business need for coupon data is worth raising with upstream as a follow-up.

proposal.rationale: Upstream added a non-contract column coupon_code to orders.csv; all 7 contract columns are present and unchanged, so meaning is unchanged. Runbook says to ignore the extra column and rerun.

applied: ingest now ignores upstream columns ['coupon_code'] on raw.orders
